sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: Passively it hears noisy components such as propellers and engines. Holding Ping suppresses passive returns; each new ping overrides the previous one, and active returns appear briefly as the echo arrives.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The sonar data composite carries up to 16 targets as pivot and pitch pairs. Sonar jammers create passive decoys.

findings.label: Sonar (Small) · tooltip
findings.value: This sensor outputs the relative angle to detected objects within its range using underwater sound waves. The sensor will passively detect certain noisy components such as propellers or engines but can also send out a loud ping to detect quiet underwater bodies. While the ping input is held passive signals will be supressed. After activating a ping additional detected signals will appear momentarily in the data channel as the signal returns to the sonar. Activating another ping will override the previous ping and no further data will be returned from the old signal.

families.summary: Cools its fluid toward the surrounding temperature at 0.003 per update, more when exposed to airflow.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: The passive radiator shares case 9 with the electric radiators and the fluid heat sink. Without a fan, its only boost is airflow: outside an enclosed compartment the multiplier becomes 1 + min(2, air speed ÷ 40).

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Connect both fluid ports; with either port unconnected the cooling step is skipped. Place it on the exterior of a moving vehicle to use the airflow term.

sections.title: Per-second rate
sections.body: At 60 updates per simulated second the passive term leaves 0.835 of the gap to ambient after one second (time constant 5.55 s). At the airflow cap the multiplier is 3, which leaves 0.581 (1.84 s).

sections.title: Volume
sections.body: The compartment volume equals the listed voxels, 9 units of 10 L.

sections.title: Flow through the radiator
sections.body:
Each update the radiator exchanges with its Fluid A network, then its Fluid B network, then cools. Arriving water is mixed by the radiator's amount after the move, and below 0.01 amount per update a direct exchange also moves temperature through the ports. Its volume is capacity: in a pumped loop it need not stay full, and its water settles cooler than the coolant manifold.

For one radiator fed at a fixed inlet temperature with flow q and stored water A, the outlet sits q ÷ (k × A + (1 + k) × q) of the way from ambient to the inlet, with k = 0.003 × (1 + fan). With 9 units of water, 200 L/s and a full fan that is 83.90 °C out for 100 °C in at 20 °C ambient, a 16.10 °C drop. The cooling capacity calculator's finite-flow mode steps whole loops.

findings.detail: Case 9 (fluid_radiator, fluid_radiator_electric, fluid_radiator_electric_5, fluid_heat_sink) moves the radiator compartment toward the surrounding temperature by this value × (1 + fan), only while both fluid ports are connected. Function 0x1403ef860-0x1403f51f4; it reads binary32 0.003 (bytes a69b443b) at 0x140baf918. Interpretation rests on retained output investigation/native/behavior/asm/water.asm:L3657-L3661 (case 9). Stored radiator temperature after the cooling step = (1 - k) × the same fraction. Example: A = 9, q = 1 ÷ 3 (200 L/s), fan 2, k = 0.009, inlet 100 °C, ambient 20 °C: outlet 83.90 °C, stored 83.32 °C, a drop of 16.10 °C across the radiator. Report: investigation/fluid-transport.md. families.summary: rudder_surface_area 8, 20, 40, 70 and 120 across the five wing sizes. The air force scales linearly with it, and the wing term lifts even at zero angle of attack.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: At the same body mass, airspeed, altitude and angle, the computed wing force scales linearly with rudder_surface_area: 8, 20, 40, 70 and 120, or 1, 2.5, 5, 8.75 and 15 times the small wing. The application cap can limit the gain on a light craft. The listed voxel count is not a multiplier.

sections.title: Wing lift
sections.body: Wing sections have rudder_type 1. On top of the normal airspeed they get a wing term 3 × c^5 × g, where c is the cosine between the direction of travel and the wing's forward axis (the reverse of dynamic_rotation_axes) and g rises from 0 at 15 m/s to 1 at 40 m/s. That term gives lift with the wing level in the airflow. Travelling backwards along that axis removes it. Wings have no Rotation input, so their angle to the airflow comes from how they are mounted and how the craft flies.

sections.title: Example
sections.body: A small wing section (area 8) on a body of mass 1000 at sea level, 30 m/s and 10° angle of attack gets a normal force of 594.2 internal units: 585.1 lift and 103.2 drag. The XXL wing makes 15 times that under the same conditions.

findings.label: Surface air velocity
findings.value: v + w × r - wind
findings.detail: The air branch takes the point velocity of the surface (body velocity plus angular velocity × lever arm, built at 0x1403e0332-0x1403e03b8) and subtracts the vehicle's cached wind here and at 0x1403e0d3d and 0x1403e0d43. Speed is in m/s, the unit established for the air scoop, which uses the same body fields. Report: investigation/control-surfaces.md. Function 0x1403dfd20-0x1403e123f; instruction bytes f3440f5c08 at 0x1403e0d38. Interpretation rests on retained output investigation/native/behavior/../control-surfaces/asm/rudder-update.asm:L846-L851. Provenance: Ghidra 12.1.4 headless, program imported with -noanalysis and only the cited routine disassembled/decompiled by a local script; this is not an REA session record.
